title: Madison Avenue Fall Gallery Walk returns with 42 elite galleries
summary: The annual Madison Avenue Fall Gallery Walk , held in association with ARTnews, is one of New York City’s most anticipated art events of the season. For one art-filled autumn day on Saturday, October 3 from 10am to 5pm, 42 internationally renowned galleries will welcome art collectors and enthusiasts to view the latest exhibitions, attend curator talks and tours, and have the opportunity to engage with artists. From the legendary masters to the contemporary artists working today, the Madison Avenue Fall Gallery Walk offers an extensive overview of the current art scene and the opportunity to see the artwork in person and to learn from artists and gallery curators. New this year, there are more new galleries to discover on Madison Avenue, as well as an Open House at Sotheby’s. Learn more about the art exhibitions on

title: Bertoia's colorful, wide-ranging Oct. 9 auction is filled with advertising, banks, toys and other sought-after objects
summary: Bertoia’s Advertising Sale on Friday, October 9, starting promptly at 10AM ET, offers a colorful mix of antique advertising, country store items and cast-iron collectibles, including soda pop, breweriana, early signs and coin-operated machines, plus 200+ still and mechanical banks, horse-drawn toys, cast-iron novelties and more. Highlights include early and graphic signs, Coca-Cola and Pepsi-Cola advertising, brewery trays and displays, clocks, tins, bottles, slot and amusement machines; and unusual store and countertop pieces. From familiar names to obscure regional brands, the auction captures the bold graphics and nostalgic imagery that once filled America’s stores, taverns and soda fountains. title: The Leiden Collection acquires its 18th Rembrandt painting
summary: The Leiden Collection, one of the world’s largest and most important private collections of 17th-century Dutch art, today announced a major milestone in its mission to preserve and disseminate Rembrandt’s legacy, adding an eighteenth painting by the iconic Old Master to its holdings: Saint John on Patmos depicting the artist’s son, Titus, as the exiled evangelist. A scholarly essay about the work and its significance — authored by Dr. Arthur K. Wheelock Jr., Senior Advisor to The Leiden Collection — was published on the Collection’s website to accompany the announcement. “From an emotional and spiritual standpoint, as well as from a scholarly perspective, Saint John on Patmos is a revelation,” Dr. Wheelock said. “Its stylistic proximity to the famous Apostles and Evangelists cycle of 1661 allows us to see Rembrandt working at the apogee of his expressive powers. title: Galerie Lelong presents Barthélémy Toguo's tenth solo show with the gallery
summary: In this new exhibition, Barthélémy Toguo presents a sensitive cartography of the contemporary world through the narrative of a constant journey – one that is simultaneously geographical, cultural and spiritual. The artist’s travels have profoundly transformed his practice. He draws upon this as a method of understanding and creation: each territory he visits becomes a place of exchange and collaboration, in which local skills, mythologies and collective memories inform his reflections on humanity and its relationship with the living world. Invited to undertake a residency in Japan last April, Toguo discovered a relationship with the world that resonated with his Cameroonian culture. In the Shinto tradition, where nature is inhabited by invisible forces, he observed similarities with the animist beliefs that shaped his childhood. title: Three sales in Paris this November for a legendary collection
summary: As France celebrates the bicentennial of photography and Paris Photo, the leading international fair dedicated to photography and the image, prepares to welcome collectors from around the world, Christie's is honoured to present more than 350 photographs from the legendary Roger Therond Collection across three sales taking place in Paris on 13 and 14 November, and online from 6 to 17 November. Roger Therond belonged to the highly exclusive circle of the five greatest photography collectors of his time, alongside figures such as Marion Lambert and Thomas Walther, a “generation of explorers with a passion for adventure.” […] They were instrumental in sparking a renewed interest in photography. “Their efforts restored to simple objects of curiosity, often neglected, the dignity and brilliance of treasures,” as Pierre Apraxine wrote in the foreword

title: Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza presents Kenny Scharf exhibition
summary: The image of Kenny Scharf (born Los Angeles, 1958) remains associated with his heyday in the 1980s in New York's East Village, where he was a friend and fellow-artist of Keith Haring and Jean-Michel Basquiat and, like them, a protégé of Andy Warhol. Scharf, however, outlived those years and his Pop-surreal aesthetic has continued to evolve and reaffirm its connection to the present day. Aspects of that aesthetic have long been overlooked. The present exhibition at the Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza aims to show how, from the outset, Scharf has also been a painter of nature and one committed to raising awareness of the climate crisis. Those who know him as a radically urban artist, enamoured with plastic and television, will be surprised to discover a hymn to nature in his work. title: Amos Rex artwork features on world star Peter Gabriel's new single cover
summary: Those walking through central Helsinki in the summer of 2022 may remember the sight: hundreds of used chairs and wooden objects hung from the roof of Lasipalatsi (Glass Palace), appearing to spill over the edge of the building towards the street. Now, Tadashi Kawamata’s The Nest has been selected for the cover of legendary musician Peter Gabriel’s single Face the Wall. The cover image was taken by photographer Mika Huisman for Amos Rex. In a comment published on his website, Gabriel says he fell in love with the work at first sight. “When I saw The Nest, I fell in love with it. To me, the wall is there, big, solid, you know, a bit like death. These messy human chairs are falling over the wall and, somehow, they spill over the top. It’s funny, but it’s also hopeful and against unbelievable odds.” Kawamata’s work was previously unfamiliar to Gabriel, but The Nest sparked his interest in the artist’s wider body of work. title: Igor Hosnedl returns to London with unsettling, metaphysical works
summary: PM/AM presents Exhibition 68, a solo presentation by Czech artist Igor Hosnedl (b. 1988, Uherské Hradiště; based in Berlin). The exhibition brings together a selection of works on paper made around 2021 with paintings from the same period and more recent works, offering a view across different moments of the artist’s practice. Exhibition 68 marks Hosnedl’s return to PM/AM following Exhibition 10. The drawings on view date from the same period as Rapunzel, Hosnedl’s 2021 solo exhibition at hunt kastner in Prague. Taking the Brothers Grimm tale as its starting point, the exhibition approached the story not as an illustration but as a way of exploring ambiguity that runs through the artist’s work: childlike naiveté alongside a sense of dread, stories that resist clear resolution. title: Cheap Trick's Rick Nielsen brings his legendary guitar collection for benefit auction
summary: Julien’s Auctions partnered with Rock & Roll Hall of Famer, acclaimed songwriter and guitarist Rick Nielsen to unveil “The Rick Nielsen Collection,” a benefit sale featuring Nielsen’s historic personal collection of guitars, cars, stage-worn wardrobe, awards, and more. The October 24 auction will benefit St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital®, an organization close to the rocker’s heart. The sale will be held live in person at Musicians Hall of Fame & Museum at the Historic Nashville Municipal Auditorium. View the auction and register to bid now at Julien’s Auctions. Nielsen’s legendary passion for guitars and collecting has resulted in an extraordinary personal archive spanning more than five decades.This landmark sale offers a rare look inside the collection of one of rock’s most beloved and entertaining guitarists. title: Josh Smith connects pop culture, repetition, and Dieter Roth in new Zurich show
summary: Galerie Eva Presenhuber is presenting Josh Smith’s (*1976) eighth solo exhibition in Zurich. One of the defining painters of his generation, Smith has developed a multifaceted body of work over more than two decades, characterized by seriality, repetition, and an ongoing engagement with the possibilities of painting. At the center of the exhibition is his recent body of work Destiny (2025), which focuses on the figure of the Grim Reaper and connects historical pictorial traditions with a contemporary visual language. The new works are complemented by paintings from 2024 as well as monotypes, works in oil on paper, and jewelry. In parallel, the gallery presents a focused selection of works by Dieter Roth, whose artistic approach has long been an important reference for Smith. title: Colnaghi London revisits how 19th-century photographers shaped the image of ancient Egypt
summary: Long before photographs of Egypt became familiar through textbooks, tourism campaigns and museum displays, making a picture beside the Nile was a slow, technically demanding process. Cameras were bulky, chemicals had to be carried through heat and dust, and every negative required careful preparation in the field. Yet it was precisely under those conditions that some of the images that helped define Europe’s visual idea of Egypt were made. A selection of those photographs is now on view at Colnaghi London as part of Out of the Sand: Ancient Egypt Rediscovered, an exhibition that brings together 19th-century photographic material documenting temples, monuments and archaeological sites across Egypt. title: Johan Creten transforms tech archaeology into art at Perrotin Paris
summary: Perrotin is presenting Les Chiens de Pavlov, the eleventh solo exhibition by Belgian artist Johan Creten with the gallery and the sixth in Paris. At once deeply personal and strikingly universal, the exhibition unfolds as an immersive journey through technological archaeology, political allegory, and mythological imagination—revealing how the dreams of yesterday continue to shape the realities of today. Johan Creten’s father had a particular obsession. Fascinated by the emerging technologies of the 1980s, he amassed, over more than four decades, a vast collection of early computers that, as the artist recalls, “occupied not only dedicated storage spaces but every available corner: stacked upon furniture, hidden behind curtains, piled one upon another in an almost archaeological density.” After his father’s death three years ago, the family inherited the machines and transformed them into a large wall, presented

title: Museum Haus Konstruktiv celebrates 40th anniversary with The Body Within Abstraction
summary: In constructivist-concrete art, the human body was largely ignored – be it as a subject, or as an element in the production of art. The focus was on the autonomy of the line, colour and surface as artistic means, whereas figurative representations were considered illusionistic and arbitrary. The group exhibition The Body Within Abstraction at Museum Haus Konstruktiv playfully and critically questions this conventional reading. Eight internationally renowned artists demonstrate how the body can serve as both a unit of measure and thematic basis for minimalistically pared-down, non-figurative art. Heidi Bucher, Eva Fàbregas, Kimsooja, Dóra Maurer, Bruce Nauman, Steven Parrino, Chiharu Shiota and Franz West: The exhibition brings together some big names, and is also a premiere, as this is the first time since moving to Löwenbräukunst-Areal that Museum Haus Konstruktiv is utilising all of its new exhibition spaces, in both the east and west wings, for a single

title: Exhibition explores photography's capacity to invent, perform, and reimagine reality
summary: The Norton Museum of Art presents Visible Fictions: Photography and Artifice, on view through February 21, 2027. The exhibition brings together more than 20 works from the Museum's Collection that challenge the notion of photography as a neutral record of reality. Through staged scenes, constructed environments, performed identities, and invented narratives, Visible Fictions reveals photography as a medium of invention as much as documentation. With images by Sophie Calle, Renée Cox, Gregory Crewdson, Thomas Demand, Tania Franco Klein, Nikki S. Lee, Cindy Sherman, Laurie Simmons, and other artists, the exhibition examines how photographs shape, rather than simply reflect, the world around us. title: Mohammad Alfaraj explores human and non-human kinship in first European solo show
summary: The heart is a bird’s nest, the brain is a spider web, the first institutional solo exhibition in Europe by Mohammad Alfaraj, brings together new commissions with recent works that reimagine the narratives shared across species and our intertwined relationships. Conceived in response to Delfina Foundation’s domestic setting, where the artist was in residence in 2018 and 2023, the exhibition unfolds across installation, drawing, photography, film, and sculpture. Among the most distinctive voices of a new generation of artists from Saudi Arabia, Alfaraj draws on social rituals, folklore, and everyday life to construct immersive narratives in which humans, animals, insects, and plants become companions, neighbours, and family. For Alfaraj, emotions, memories, and the stories we tell ourselves are woven from different threads: some lived, some imagined.

title: ROM transforms main-floor space with new artwork by French-Caribbean artist Raphaël Barontini
summary: This fall, visitors to the Royal Ontario Museum are being greeted by a breathtaking large-scale montage that completely transforms the Museum's main-floor gallery. ROM unveiled Unbound: The Allegorical Archipelago of Abya Yala, an original work by celebrated French-Caribbean artist Raphaël Barontini, on view in the Hyacinth Gloria Chen Court from September 26, 2026, to August 29, 2027, as part of the 2026 Toronto Biennial of Art – the first time the Museum has participated in the Biennial. Visitors can view the installation free of charge during ROM's Free Main Floor pilot from September 25 to November 30, 2026, making this new artwork accessible to all. title: The Contemporary Dayton presents landmark Appalachia project by Stacy Kranitz
summary: The Contemporary Dayton is presenting Stacy Kranitz: Ain’t No Grave Gonna Hold My Body Down, a landmark multi-year project by Pulitzer Prize–winning photographer Stacy Kranitz that challenges long-held stereotypes and assumptions about Appalachia. Opening as part of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial: The Long View, the exhibition brings together more than 40 photographs alongside historical archival materials, texts, installation, and a world-premiere film, produced by FilmDayton. Together, these works examine how Appalachia has been represented—and misrepresented—across generations, asking who has had the power to shape the story of the region and what is revealed when those narratives are reconsidered. Kranitz’s project explores Appalachia as a place shaped by myth, exploitation, resilience, and resistance. Her photographs

title: Sunderland student lands dream role at landmark venue
summary: A University of Sunderland student who travelled to the UK from his home in Kuwait to pursue a career in the arts has landed his dream role within the city's new major landmark, Culture House Sunderland. The multi-purpose venue, which officially opened its doors in Keel Square on September 12, features a library, exhibition and events spaces, bar and podcast studio. It is also the new home for the University’s Northern Gallery for Contemporary Art (NGCA). And there to welcome visitors to the gallery is 27-year-old MA Design and Illustration student, Sullivan (Sully) Alenezi-Bonney, who recently began the role of Gallery Learning Facilitator. Sully designs, coordinates, and delivers educational programmes that connect diverse audiences – from school groups and families to adults – with the gallery's collections and exhibitions. title: MOT explores Taiwan-Japan Avant-Garde exchange in Synchronic Constellation
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo is presenting Synchronic Constellation: Cross-Boundary Perspectives in Art, an exhibition that reconsiders the cultural and artistic modernity of Taiwan and Japan. The show draws inspiration from a film on the Le Moulin Poetry Society, a collective of modernist writers founded in Taiwan in the 1930s. Featuring approximately 200 modern Taiwanese artworks, 500 related archival materials, and 100 contemporaneous Japanese pieces, the exhibition maps a constellation of intercultural exchange, inviting viewers to rethink modernity through from today’s vantage point. title: Centro de Arte Moderna Gulbenkian presents fall 2026 exhibitions
summary: Centro de Arte Moderna Gulbenkian kicks off the season with two exhibitions that propose new ways of imagining the world. The Exhibition of a Dream, by Mathieu Copeland, transforms real dreams into a sound experience, taking over the Engawa Space. Murky Waters, by Inês Zenha, presents sculptures and installations made of adobe, ceramics, and water, giving shape to hybrid bodies and subterranean landscapes. In the Main Gallery at the headquarters, Centro de Arte Moderna Gulbenkian presents Painting Is Easy. Do It Yourself!. Curated by João Maria Gusmão, the exhibition brings together works from the la Caixa Foundation’s Contemporary Art Collection that question the role of art today. title: NADA welcomes 19 new members to its international network
summary: NADA has welcomed 19 new members into its international network of galleries, nonprofit organizations and artist-run spaces, expanding a community that now includes more than 280 members working across the contemporary art field. The Fall 2026 group reflects the organization’s increasingly broad geographic reach, bringing together spaces from major art centers including New York, Los Angeles, Miami, Chicago, Montreal, Prague, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok, as well as organizations based in cities such as Boulder, Richmond, Concord and Portland, Maine. According to NADA, the new additions are part of its continuing effort to broaden the range of voices represented within its membership and to support galleries and organizations working with contemporary artists in different regions and at different scales.

title: Contemporary figurative works meet modern history
summary: The exhibition From the Sleep Side presents a cross-generational and transcontinental survey of three artists, placing contemporary figurative painting in a historical dialogue. It focuses on new works by the US American artist Aubrey Levinthal (b. 1986) whose recent paintings are placed in a direct visual and thematic relationship with works by Biala (Janice Biala, 1903—2000) and Tal R (b. 1967), both of whom serve as significant points of reference and sources of inspiration for Levinthal. The poet Anne Carson once described a disorienting dream about entering her living room at night to find all the lights on. Nothing was wrong, everything was in its usual place, »and yet it was utterly, certainly, different«. title: ICA London presents Autumn Knight's UK institutional debut
summary: The Institute of Contemporary Arts (ICA) London presents a new commission and recent work by New York-based artist Autumn Knight, marking the first major presentation of her work in the UK. Knight’s interdisciplinary practice draws on theatre, psychology, improvisation and social exchange. Titled I Can’t Complain, her solo exhibition at the ICA presents a new installation and performance work about the act of complaining: its pleasures, its frustrations, and its political potential. At a moment when questions of voice, authority, and participation are increasingly contested, I Can’t Complain opens a dialogue with audiences about how power is negotiated in everyday life, asking not how we can stop complaining, but what complaints make visible.
